summary:
Result of the independent check: both points are closed, and the lane has no decision. `decisions.json` is now `[]`. The ids D-PRE-51 and D-PRE-52 stay free. Skills in use: ariakit-general-workflow, ariakit-general-markdown, ariakit-ariakit-api-design.

The largest change: I withdrew D-PRE-52 (point B). The author recommended the lab rule (no memory). But the maintainer selected the rule of today three times, and D-WORK-03 keeps it. A corrected form of the decision is in `withdrawn/` for the case that you want to ask.

Files, all below /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/round7/decisions/two-points:
- decisions.json: `[]`.
- closed.md: point A (parts A1 to A6) and point B (parts B1 to B7), with what the implementation must do.
- fragments/CLOSED-run-approval-large.html and fragments/CLOSED-open-variant.html: record text with no panel.
- withdrawn/D-PRE-52.json and withdrawn/D-PRE-52.html: not a part of the result.
- notes.md: each check, each correction, 11 doubts.
- check/author-original/: the author files, copied first. check/checker-scripts/, check/checker-docs/, check/checker-lab-probe.json, check/trial-final/, check/trial-withdrawn/, check/checker-shots/.

Checks (measured): `node apps/lab/audit/build.mjs --strict --content <copy of backup-r7> --out <out>` passes with no warning for both trials (58 decisions, and 59 with the withdrawn decision). `check.mjs --only standalone` passes 37 checks at 1440 px and 37 at 400 px for each. The worktree status is the same before and after. No commit, no GitHub write, no request to production. The lab probe sent GET requests only.

What I verified again: each cited code line (2 citations were wrong), the 5 Cloudflare pages (downloaded again, byte for byte equal), the saved D1 probe results, pull request #104 (`gh pr view`), D04 and U03 in the saved audit files, and the lab behavior with another key sequence.

POINT B, why it is closed. The author found a true new fact: the lab page has no memory (measured again: 3, Down, Up shows Chromium, Light). The lab page selects the variant itself and does not use the memory of its session hook:

```ts
// apps/lab/src/explorations/pages/review/ariakit/model.ts:72-78 (no memory)
item.variants.find((variant) => variant.status === "needs-review") ??
  item.variants.find(isCoverVariant) ?? item.variants[0]
// apps/web/src/review/review-workspace.tsx:359-362 (the keys of today)
next.variants.find((entry) => entry.key === previous) ??
  next.variants.find(needsReview) ?? next.variants[0]
```

But the rule is settled (counted): D04 selected "Remember the last variant for each item" and not "Always open the first variant". Pull request #104 of the maintainer (commit 859ad6f, 2026-09-27) says "Routed item links always select the first variant needing review" and "Keyboard item navigation can restore the last explicitly chosen variant for that item". U03, which contract line 144 keeps, says "Item links target the first pending variant; remembered keyboard selection remains separate." D-WORK-03 keeps "the keys of today", and the issue review-frame has the acceptance line "Each does what it does today". Contract line 5 says "An unselected question or a passing source check does not change the contract", and no lab question named this rule. So the lab difference is a defect that the move repairs.

POINT A stays closed, with three corrections in the implementation list (see corrections).
closed: Point A, the run approval of a large run: closed by D-WORK-04 ("in one transaction", "one Undo reverses the command"), by D-SCALE-02 (a stated limit of changed captures, nothing built now, parts not selected, note "Let's defer this to when this is a problem."), and by the D1 rule that a batch rolls back as a whole (https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/#batch). Details: /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/round7/decisions/two-points/closed.md, parts A1 to A6.

Point A, the facts (verified again). Counted from code: no page sends more than one screenshot in a command today, and a batch that D1 refuses is tried up to 5 times and then answers HTTP 409 with the code "conflict" (apps/web/src/operations/review-queue.ts:62 and :147-156, apps/web/src/api/review.ts:812-830). Measured (document read, https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/platform/limits/, last change 2026-04-21): 30 seconds for a query and for the entire batch call, no count of rows for one batch, and the rough guideline "hundreds of thousands of rows or hundreds of MBs". Calculation from local D1 values of the audit: 20,000 changes are 100,008 rows with 80,000 rows and 38.6 MB in the largest statement. The lowest count of the D1 words is 25,000 changes. A run cannot reach it while the capture limit is about 20,000. The time on production D1 is not known.

Point A, what the implementation must do in step 3 of the issue review-decisions: (1) one D1 batch, so a refused approval saves no decision row and no code for parts exists; (2) the run approval is a stored decision as each other (D-RES-06), so the accepted row 12 of D-OPS-01 applies with no new rule: a wait between the attempts, 5 attempts at most, the state "dead", an own error code in place of "conflict", and the Status page reads the dead tasks; (3) for a run approval with that code, the status line says that nothing was saved and names the next step, with no cause that the server does not know (proposal: "Not saved. The approval of the run failed. Approve one screenshot at a time, or try again."); (4) the same for the Undo of a run approval (measured on a local D1 by the audit: 11,505 rows for 3,832 targets); (5) the test of the issue stays. Permitted and not necessary: end the tries at the first of the three D1 errors of the error list (timeout, memory, CPU). It must not build a limit of changes, a menu item that is off above a count, a state "approval in progress", or a test write to production D1.
Point A, when it opens again (a reading, not a text of the record): the first refusal of a run approval in production, or the pull request that sets the capture limit of one run above 25,000.

Point B, the variant that a screenshot opens on: closed by the earlier decision D04, pull request #104 of the maintainer (2026-09-27), the earlier decision U03 (contract line 144), D-WORK-03 (the keys of today), and contract line 5. The settled rule is the rule of the app of today: a click on a row and a link with no variant open the first variant that needs review, and Up and Down open the variant that the reviewer selected last in that screenshot (on a first visit: the first variant that needs review). Example: on ariakit-ui-button/page/default the reviewer presses 3 (Firefox, Light), Down, Up. The settled rule shows Firefox, Light. The lab page shows Chromium, Light (measured two times). Details: closed.md, parts B1 to B7.
